paper.title_en: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
paper.abstract_en: At strong repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto states without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments on the square lattice and, where possible, any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on $N\geq2$ sites, $μ_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$ for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $μ_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count $P_{\rm same}$ (four hops move at most three particles). For uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$, $μ_4=A+αP_{\rm same}$ in closed form: the slope $α=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$ is set by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles, the intercept, via hard-core bosons, by edge, edge-pair and 4-cycle counts. With arbitrary Peierls phases, $μ_4$ is a spin-independent baseline plus a coefficient times $\sum_C\cosΘ_C$ over 4-cycle Wilson phases. (3) At finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Exchange loops carry the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, $α\cosΦ_\square$ on $L\times L$ tori, $L\neq4$, while the doublon hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $π$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows up to $O((2λ)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the closed form in (2) without phases, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moments and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.
